If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

This event will not happen right after Yahweh plucks up these nations. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [And it will happen that a long time after I pluck them up, I will turn and have compassion on them and bring them back, a man to his inheritance and a man to his land]

The phrase **turn and have compassion** expresses a single idea. The word **turn** tells more about **have compassion**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [I will once more have compassion on them]

Yahweh is using **a man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “each person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [each person to his inheritance and each person to his land]

Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that these nations will learn the ways of his people and swear by his name. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [if they truly learn the ways of my people, so that they swear by my name ‘As Yahweh lives,’ just as they have taught my people to swear by Baal, then I will build them up in the midst of my people]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **learn** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [if they truly learn]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [to swear by my name that Yahweh lives]
See how you translated this phrase in [5:2](../05/02.md).

The expression **they will be built** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [then I will build them up in the midst of my people]

Here Yahweh is speaking of making these nations secure and prosperous among his people as if they were a house that he **built**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then they will become accepted and prosperous in the midst of my people]
